fact_text: Before Adrien leaves Singapore, his employer must seek tax clearance by filing Form IR21 with IRAS at least one month before his last day of employment (or before he goes on an overseas posting or leaves Singapore for more than three months), and may withhold his final monies until clearance is given.
evidence_quote: Employers must file Form IR21 at least one month before a non-Singapore Citizen employee ceases employment in Singapore, goes on an overseas posting, or leaves Singapore for more than three months.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Host-exit obligation. Tax clearance is the employer's duty, triggered on exit; the employer withholds final salary/bonus/leave pay until IRAS clears. Adrien should coordinate his last-day and final-pay timing around this. IRAS pages are JS-rendered so re-confirm verbatim before use.

fact_text: When Adrien stops working in Singapore, his employer must cancel his Employment Pass - within one week from the departure date if he has left permanently - and any Dependant's Passes issued to his family are cancelled at the same time.
evidence_quote: If the pass holder has left Singapore permanently, you must cancel the EP within 1 week from the departure date, unless it has expired. Once the pass is cancelled, all related passes issued to family members will also be cancelled.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Host-exit obligation. Cancelling the EP also cancels the family's Dependant's Passes - the family loses valid stay at the same moment. If anyone needs to remain in Singapore briefly after cancellation, the employer can request a Short-Term Visit Pass (up to 90 days) to avoid overstaying.

fact_text: As an Employment Pass holder Adrien had no CPF account, because mandatory CPF is only for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents - so there is no CPF balance to close, transfer or withdraw when he repatriates.
evidence_quote: CPF contributions are payable for Singapore citizens (SCs) and Singapore permanent residents (SPRs) who are: Working in Singapore under a contract of service.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Host-exit clarification. Unlike departing PRs, an EP holder has no CPF to unwind on exit. There is also no France-Singapore social security totalization agreement, so his Singapore period does not accrue transferable French pension/health entitlements - flag for retirement planning.

fact_text: In the year Adrien returns to live in France, he must promptly inform the non-residents tax office (Service des impots des particuliers non-residents) of his new French address, and file his return the following year (the return for 2025 income is filed in spring 2026).
evidence_quote: L'année de votre retour en France, vous devez informer rapidement le service des impôts des particuliers non-résidents de votre nouvelle adresse.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Home-re-entry obligation. The returning expat still deals with the non-residents tax office in the transition year; that office then forwards the file to the tax office of the new French domicile.

fact_text: On returning to France, Adrien should check and adapt his prelevement a la source (withholding) rate in his online tax account; if he does not set a personalised rate, a default (non-personalised) rate that ignores his family situation is applied, which can lead to over-withholding.
evidence_quote: Vérifiez votre taux de prélèvement à la source dans votre espace en ligne. Si vous ne disposez pas d'un taux personnalisé, les services fiscaux vous appliquent un taux non personnalisé (appelé taux par défaut).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Home-re-entry, easy to miss. A returning expat has no active PAS rate on file, so a default bracket rate (0%-43%) applies until he sets a personalised rate online. Failing to adapt it risks paying an excess that is only refunded much later.

fact_text: For the year he returns, Adrien files declaring his French-source income taxable in France received from 1 January up to his return date, and then his worldwide (French and foreign) income received from the return date to 31 December; on paper this is form 2042-NR plus form 2042.
evidence_quote: Formulaire n°2042-NR pour vos revenus de source française imposables en France perçus du 1er janvier à la date de votre retour en France Formulaire n°2042 pour tous vos revenus perçus de la date de votre retour en France jusqu'au 31 décembre.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Home-re-entry. The return year is split: non-resident treatment (French-source only) up to the return date, then full resident (worldwide) treatment after. Adrien must also declare any foreign accounts held while abroad.

fact_text: To reopen French health cover on his return, Adrien (if he resumes work in France) is affiliated to French Assurance maladie from the first hour worked; he opens his rights by sending a copy of his employment contract or a payslip together with form S1106 (PUMa) to the CPAM of his place of residence, then updates his carte Vitale.
evidence_quote: Pour faire ouvrir vos droits, vous devez envoyer par courrier une copie du contrat de travail ou d'un bulletin de salaire accompagné du formulaire S1106 (demande d'ouverture de droit à la protection universelle maladie - Puma) à la CPAM de votre lieu de résidence.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Home-re-entry. Coverage is not automatic on landing - it must be requested via S1106. The verbatim procedure above is stated on the Service-Public page for returns from the EEE/EU/Switzerland/UK; Adrien is returning from Singapore (a non-EEA country), where the same professional-activity affiliation applies, but if he is NOT working he faces the general PUMa condition of 3 months' stable, continuous residence before rights open.
